PC:
Prepares an appropriate operation room set-up for performing deep sedation:
Places nasal cannula with end-tidal CO2 monitoring capability
Has appropriate size bag and mask, handle and blade, LMA, and endotracheal tube available
Places standard ASA monitors appropriately

Administers deep sedation with assistance:
Chooses the sedative and both the appropriate dose and route for administration
Might titrate the sedation to effect as needed
Verbalizes that the patient is apneic
Tries to arouse patient using verbal and/or tactile stimulation

Initiates management under supervision:
Performs chin lift and bag mask ventilation

Performs more specific management for the complication:
Administers sedation reversal if appropriate

Identifies and manages complications that are patient, surgery and anesthetic related in a cohesive fashion and maintains conditional independence:
Provides appropriate airway management which may include bag valve mask ventilation, LMA, or endotracheal tube
Learner should assess patient, including brief assessment of airway, cardiovascular, pulmonary, and neurologic systems.
Learner should provide oxygen to the patient via mask or nasal cannula, ideally with end tidal CO2 monitoring in place.
Learner should outline a plan for sedation for the retrobulbar block and prepare to administer the sedation.
Learner should choose sedation with a variety of agents including propofol, midazolam, fentanyl, alfentanil, or other.
Learner should administer sedation or other comfort measures.
Learner should continue to monitor the patient during the block.
Learner should identify somnolence, apnea, desaturation, hypotension, and bradycardia.
Learner should attempt mask ventilation of the patient.
Learner should obtain definitive airway management via either placement of an LMA or endotracheal intubation with or without paralytic.
Learner should administer alpha or beta agonists to improve hemodynamics.
MK: Verbalizes a plan for deep but short lasting sedation for the procedure
Verbalizes likely diagnosis of intrathecal injection as a complication of retrobulbar block
Verbalize that intrathecal injection can result in high spinal
Can list differential diagnosis of apnea after deep sedation and retrobulbar block
Can explain the pathophysiology and management of high spinal after retrobulbar block almost independently.
Demonstrates an expert level knowledge about the retrobulbar and peribulbar blocks, their complications and its management.
Learner should identify retrobulbar block as source of high spinal.
SBP:
Performs all of the above independently and plays a leader role in coordinating care:
Verbalizes a plan for patient’s disposition and monitoring
Learner should ask that CPR and ACLS be started.
Learner should request crash cart brought into the OR and paddles placed on patient.
ICS: Introduces self to the surgical team at the beginning of procedure
Clearly communicates with the surgeon regarding apnea and need to support ventilation
Discusses patient’s condition and treatment options with the surgeon and with the anesthesia staff
Plays a team leader role in management
Gives clear instructions to other team members in a non-threatening calm manner if assistance is needed (e.g. squeeze the bag once every 6 seconds while I am providing a two hand-mask)
Gives positive feedback to other team members (e.g. good job squeezing that bag)
Learner should inform the surgeons when the patient is appropriately sedated to perform the block.
